questions.text: Derive the Friis transmission formula for free space radio communication: $P_r = P_t G_t G_r \left(\frac{\lambda}{4\pi d}\right)^2$. A microwave link operates at $2.8\text{ GHz}$ over $70\text{ km}$ distance with antenna gains of $20\text{ dB}$ at both ends and transmitted power of $10\text{ W}$. Calculate the received signal power.

Explain the mechanism of ionospheric wave propagation and its structure (D, E, F1, F2 layers). Define critical frequency ($f_c$), virtual height, skip distance ($d_{\text{skip}}$), and Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF). Derive the Secant Law: $\text{MUF} = f_c \sec\theta_i = f_c \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{d}{2h}\right)^2}$.

Explain the construction, working principle, current distribution, and radiation pattern of a Yagi-Uda Antenna array. What is the role of the driven folded dipole element, reflector, and directors? Design a 5-element Yagi-Uda antenna.

Explain the working principle, geometry, design parameters (scaling factor $\tau$ and spacing factor $\sigma$), advantages, and applications of a Log-Periodic Dipole Array (LPDA) antenna. Why is it broadband?

Explain the following antenna parameters with definitions and mathematical relations: (a) Radiation Pattern and Half-Power Beamwidth (HPBW), (b) Directivity and Antenna Gain ($G = \eta D$), (c) Radiation Resistance and Input Impedance, (d) Antenna Polarization (Linear, Circular, Elliptical).

Derive an expression for the total electric field and array factor in the case of two isotropic point sources with equal amplitude and arbitrary phase difference $\alpha$. Distinguish between Broadside Array and End-Fire Array with radiation patterns.
What is an aperture antenna? Explain the construction, working principle, feed mechanisms, and radiation characteristics of Parabolic Reflector Antennas, Cassegrain feed systems, and Horn antennas.
State and explain fundamental antenna theorems: (a) Reciprocity Theorem, (b) Compensation Theorem, and (c) Maximum Power Transfer Theorem.
What is Retarded Potential and Retarded Time? Explain the radiation mechanism of a Hertzian dipole and derive the electric and magnetic field components in the radiation far-field zone.

Describe space wave propagation and the Two-Ray Ground Reflection model. Explain the effect of earth curvature on the radio horizon and calculate the maximum Line-of-Sight (LOS) distance: $d = 4.12(\sqrt{h_t} + \sqrt{h_r})\text{ km}$.
Explain Ground (Surface) Wave propagation over plane and spherical earth. Discuss Sommerfeld's numerical distance and factors causing severe attenuation of surface waves at higher frequencies.
Explain Tropospheric Wave propagation. Describe Tropospheric Scatter communication, atmospheric duct propagation (surface and elevated ducts), and abnormal refraction.
Explain Knife-Edge Diffraction phenomenon and Fresnel Zones. How is diffraction loss calculated using the Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction parameter $v = h\sqrt{\frac{2(d_1+d_2)}{\lambda d_1 d_2}}$?
Explain the construction, working principle, radiation characteristics, and non-resonant matched termination of a Rhombic Antenna.
What is Acceptance Angle? Derive the expression for Numerical Aperture ($\text{NA} = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2}$) of a step-index optical fiber. Explain attenuation and chromatic dispersion mechanisms.
Write short notes on: (a) Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP), (b) Microstrip Patch Antenna, (c) Folded Dipole Antenna, (d) Marconi Monopole Antenna.

Derive the radiation resistance $R_{rad} = 80\pi^2 (dl/\lambda)^2$, radiated power $P_{rad}$, and magnetic vector potential $\vec{A}$ of an infinitesimal Hertzian Dipole antenna carrying current $I(t) = I_0 \cos(\omega t)$.
questions.solutionOutline: Retarded vector potential A_z = (mu I_0 dl / 4 pi r) e^(-j beta r). Far fields: E_theta = j (eta I_0 dl beta / 4 pi r) sin(theta) e^(-j beta r), H_phi = E_theta / eta. Poynting vector S_r = 0.5 Re[E x H*]. Integrate over sphere: P_rad = 40 pi^2 I_0^2 (dl/lambda)^2. Radiation resistance R_rad = 2 P_rad / I_0^2 = 80 pi^2 (dl/lambda)^2.

questions.text: Derive the electric field radiation pattern, input impedance ($Z_{in} \approx 73 + j42.5\ \Omega$), and directivity ($D = 1.64$ or $2.15\text{ dBi}$) of a center-fed Half-Wave Dipole antenna.
questions.solutionOutline: Current distribution I(z) = I_0 cos(beta z) for -lambda/4 <= z <= lambda/4. Far electric field E_theta = j (60 I_0 / r) e^(-j beta r) [cos((pi/2) cos theta) / sin theta]. Half-power beamwidth HPBW = 78 degrees. Radiated power P_rad = 36.56 I_0^2 => R_rad = 73.13 ohms. Radiation intensity U_max = 60 I_0^2 / (2 pi) => Directivity D = 4 pi U_max / P_rad = 1.643 (2.15 dBi).

questions.text: Explain Broadside Array and End-Fire Array of $N$ isotropic point sources with uniform spacing $d$ and progressive phase shift $\alpha$. Derive the array factor $AF = \frac{\sin(N\psi/2)}{N\sin(\psi/2)}$, null directions, and directivity expressions.
questions.solutionOutline: Total field E = Element factor x Array Factor. psi = beta d cos(theta) + alpha. Sum of geometric progression yields AF = sin(N psi / 2) / (N sin(psi / 2)). Broadside: maximum radiation at theta = 90 degrees => alpha = 0. End-fire: maximum radiation along array axis theta = 0 or 180 degrees => alpha = -beta d or +beta d.

questions.text: Explain the Hansen-Woodyard condition for enhanced directivity in end-fire arrays. Derive the required progressive phase shift $\alpha = -\left(\beta d + \frac{\pi}{N}\right)$ and discuss its limitations.
questions.solutionOutline: Ordinary end-fire array sets psi = 0 at theta = 0 (alpha = -beta d). Hansen-Woodyard showed directivity increases by factor of ~1.78 by requiring terminal phase difference |psi|_{theta=pi} = pi and setting alpha = -(beta d + pi / N). Requires close spacing d < lambda/2.

questions.text: State and prove the Pattern Multiplication Theorem. Sketch polar radiation patterns of a two-element array and a four-element uniform linear array using pattern multiplication.
questions.solutionOutline: Pattern Multiplication states that total radiation pattern of an array of identical antennas equals vector product of individual element pattern and the array factor of isotropic elements located at identical positions: E_total(theta, phi) = E_element(theta, phi) * AF(theta, phi). Greatly simplifies multi-element directional array synthesis.

questions.text: Explain the operation, physical structure, and design principles of the Yagi-Uda Antenna (Driven element, Reflector, Directors). Calculate beamwidth, front-to-back ratio, and forward gain.
questions.solutionOutline: Parasitic end-fire directional array widely used for VHF/UHF TV reception. Driven element: folded dipole (~0.47 lambda, input impedance ~300 ohms). Reflector: ~5% longer (~0.5 lambda) spaced 0.15-0.2 lambda behind driven element, inductive impedance. Directors: ~5% shorter (~0.45 lambda) spaced 0.2-0.3 lambda in front, capacitive impedance. Provides high forward gain (10-15 dBi) and high front-to-back ratio.

questions.text: Describe the Helical Antenna operating in Normal Mode and Axial (End-Fire) Mode. Derive pitch angle $\alpha = \arctan(S / \pi D)$, input impedance $R \approx 140 C_\lambda$, beamwidth, and circular polarization conditions.
questions.solutionOutline: Conducting wire wound in helical coil over ground plane. Normal mode (D << lambda): radiation perpendicular to helix axis, linear or elliptical polarization, low efficiency. Axial mode (C = pi D ~ lambda, alpha ~ 12-14 degrees): highly directional end-fire beam along helix axis, pure circular polarization, input impedance purely resistive R ~ 140 (C / lambda) ohms, broad bandwidth.

questions.text: Explain Microstrip Patch Antennas. Formulate design equations for resonant frequency $f_r$, effective dielectric constant $\epsilon_{reff}$, physical length $L$, and fringe field extension $\Delta L$. List advantages and disadvantages.
questions.solutionOutline: Metallic patch printed on thin dielectric substrate backed by continuous ground plane. Effective dielectric constant eps_reff = (eps_r + 1)/2 + (eps_r - 1)/2 * [1 + 12 h/W]^(-0.5). Resonant length L = c / (2 f_r sqrt(eps_reff)) - 2 Delta L. Advantages: low profile, lightweight, conformal, easily integrated with MMIC. Disadvantages: narrow bandwidth (1-5%), low efficiency, lower power handling.

questions.text: Explain Parabolic Reflector Antennas. Discuss feed mechanisms (Cassegrain, Gregorian, Prime Focus, Offset), aperture efficiency ($\eta$), spillover, blockage, and calculate gain $G = \eta \left(\frac{\pi D}{\lambda}\right)^2$ and 3-dB beamwidth.
questions.solutionOutline: Parabolic surface transforms spherical wavefront from focal point feed into planar wavefront across aperture. Cassegrain feed uses hyperboloidal subreflector at focal point; Gregorian uses ellipsoidal subreflector. Eliminates long waveguide runs. Gain G = eta (pi D / lambda)^2. Beamwidth HPBW ~ 70 lambda / D degrees. Offset feed eliminates aperture blockage and minimizes sidelobes.

questions.text: Explain Horn Antennas: E-plane sectoral, H-plane sectoral, and Pyramidal horn. Derive optimum horn dimensions for maximum gain and discuss impedance matching from waveguide to free space.
questions.solutionOutline: Flared waveguide acting as impedance transformer between wave impedance of guide (TE10 mode) and free space (377 ohms). Flaring in electric field direction produces E-plane sectoral horn; flaring in magnetic field direction produces H-plane sectoral horn; flaring in both directions produces Pyramidal horn. Optimum horn balances aperture size gain increase against quadratic phase error loss.

questions.text: Explain Ground Wave (Surface Wave) Propagation. Discuss Earth curvature attenuation, ground conductivity ($\sigma$) and permittivity ($\epsilon_r$), and wave tilt during surface wave propagation.
questions.solutionOutline: Diffracts around Earth curvature guided between conductive Earth surface and atmosphere (used for VLF, LF, MF AM broadcast). Ground losses increase rapidly with frequency (impractical above 2 MHz). Wave tilt occurs because electrical conductivity is finite, causing electric field vectors to tilt forward, transferring energy into ground losses.

questions.text: Explain Line-of-Sight (LOS) Space Wave Propagation. Derive the path loss formula including direct and ground-reflected rays, radio horizon distance $d \approx 4.12(\sqrt{h_t} + \sqrt{h_r})\text{ km}$, and effective Earth radius factor ($k = 4/3$).
questions.solutionOutline: Space waves propagate directly through troposphere for VHF/UHF/Microwaves. Total field is vector sum of direct ray and ground-reflected ray. For grazing angles: E_r approx 2 E_0 sin(2 pi h_t h_r / lambda d) approx E_0 (4 pi h_t h_r / lambda d^2). Power falls off as 1/d^4. Atmospheric refraction bends rays toward Earth, modeled by equivalent Earth radius R' = k R where k = 4/3.

questions.text: Explain Critical Frequency ($f_c$), Maximum Usable Frequency ($MUF = f_c \sec \theta_i$), Skip Distance ($D_{skip}$), and Virtual Height in ionospheric sky wave propagation. Calculate MUF for given plasma density and incident angle.
questions.solutionOutline: Ionosphere ionizes into D, E, F1, F2 layers. Critical frequency f_c = 9 sqrt(N_max) is highest frequency reflected at vertical incidence. At oblique incidence angle theta_i: Secant law MUF = f_c / cos(theta_i) = f_c sec(theta_i). Skip distance is minimum distance from transmitter at which sky wave of given frequency returns to Earth. Virtual height is apparent reflection height determined from pulse echo delay.

questions.text: Explain Optical Wave Propagation through step-index optical fiber waveguides: Total Internal Reflection, Numerical Aperture ($NA = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2}$), normalized frequency ($V$-number), and modal dispersion in step-index vs graded-index fibers.
questions.solutionOutline: Light guides through silica core (n1) by total internal reflection at cladding (n2 < n1) boundary when theta > theta_c = arcsin(n2/n1). Numerical Aperture NA = sin(theta_a) = sqrt(n1^2 - n2^2). Normalized frequency V = (2 pi a / lambda) * NA; single-mode condition V < 2.405. Step-index fibers suffer intermodal dispersion; parabolic graded-index fibers equalize transit time of modal rays.
